title: Studies in the History of the Renaissance

title: Marius the Epicurean: His Sensations and Ideas
description: Published in 1885 and Pater's only completed novel: the education of a young Roman of the second century as he passes from Epicureanism through the cult of Cybele to the Christian church. It is a prose fiction work of 1885 by Walter Pater; it belongs to Aestheticism and the Decadent Decade and it is catalogued here under novel of development and the growth story; realist novel of common life and the record grades it as major canon and its author standing in the first rank of this corpus.
plot_or_argument: Marius, a thoughtful Roman boy of the age of the Antonines, passes from the old household religion of his family's villa and the healing temple of Aesculapius, through the Cyrenaic philosophy of sensation shared with his friend Flavian, to the Stoicism of Marcus Aurelius's court; drawn by the Christian soldier Cornelius and the household of the saintly Cecilia, he gives himself up in his friend's place when Christians are arrested, and dies of fever among them, honoured as a martyr though never baptised.
narrative_structure: A novel in chapters grouped by the stages of a life, from childhood through the education and the first disappointments to the settlement of the adult. A novel in chapters, the action carried in sequence from the opening situation to the closing resolution, with the material world of the household described at length.

meter_and_prosody: Prose.
